newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: AEGON SAYS STOCK MARKET, STRONG Q4 BOOST 96 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: AEGON SAYS STOCK MARKET, STRONG Q4 BOOST 96 PROFIT.

text.p: Insurer Aegon NV said on Friday buoyant stock markets and an exceptionally strong fourth quarter helped lift its net profit by 18.5 percent to 1.568 billion guilders in 1996 from 1.323 billion in 1995.

"The full year's net income showed a higher than expected increase, due to an exceptionally good fourth quarter operationally, favourable stock market conditions and the strengthening of Aegon's main currencies," it said.
Aegon said it had achieved double-digit growth of pre-tax profits in all four of its main business areas in 1996.
Life insurance posted a 15 percent rise, accident and health insurance profits were up 13 percent, general insurance earnings advanced 61 percent while banking profits rose 16 percent.
Aegon said 1996 earnings were boosted in part by the appreciation of the dollar and sterling against the guilder, particularly in the final quarter of the year.
U.S. earnings rose 14.2 percent in dollars but 20 percent in guilders. Earnings of Aegon's Scottish Equitable unit grew 24 percent in sterling terms.
Aegon chairman Kees Storm described 1996 as a year of high-quality growth, adding that he was confident 1997 would be another good year.

"Through well considered acquisitions and divestments we further focused our portfolio on our core businesses. But most importantly we managed to maintain solid organic growth in all out major markets," he said.
